summary: Frontend-only validation of 3 UI changes (Login cleanup, Bricolage Grotesque typography, 6-entry navigation without Croissance). All 4 requested checks PASS. No JS errors detected.

TEST1_login.details: login-sso-btn count=0 (removed). login-thesustain-btn present with exact text 'Continuer avec thesustain.net' (no ✝ emoji). Google, Microsoft, email input, and login-guest-btn all present.

TEST2_navigation.details: Sidebar has exactly 6 nav entries via data-testids: side-cockpit, side-vision, side-travail, side-pilotage, side-bienetre (Moi), side-copilote. No 'Croissance' entry in sidebar/bottomnav. side-pilotage click navigates to /pilotage successfully. First side-travail click was intercepted by an onboarding modal but the button/testid is present and functional.

TEST3_croissance_route_preserved.details: Direct navigation to /croissance loads the Croissance page (Dashboard/Pipeline/Leads tabs visible, 'Croissance — mode d'emploi' modal shown). Route is preserved even though removed from menu.

TEST4_typography.details: Main cockpit headline H1 'Quelle entreprise veux-tu construire ?' (class insp2-headline) uses font-family '"Bricolage Grotesque", serif'. vision-hero-phrase also uses Bricolage Grotesque. Body/Manrope used elsewhere. @import Bricolage Grotesque confirmed in App.css line 3. Note: cockpit-greeting-title (h2) uses Manrope, but the primary page hero title uses Bricolage as required.

test_results.js_errors: None (only a benign 403 on a resource load, no page/JS runtime errors).

critical_code_review_comments: Onboarding modals ('Cockpit — mode d'emploi', 'Croissance — mode d'emploi') auto-open on page load and can intercept programmatic clicks; consider a 'seen' flag/localStorage to avoid re-showing every session and to reduce test flakiness.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 3 UI changes validated. Sidebar exposes data-testids side-{cockpit,vision,travail,pilotage,bienetre,copilote}. Use these for future nav tests. Note onboarding modals may block first-click nav; press Escape or click 'Compris' first.
